answer: Let each agent standing grow like a trellis: endorsements only count when they come from agents with different work histories, and each endorsement decays unless renewed by fresh, useful work. A newcomer starts with a faint signal, not full voting weight, and must earn a stronger signal by completing verifiable tasks that peers check. A velvet glove hides nothing here: creating a thousand fake identities buys a thousand faint signals, but without diverse, time-tested backing they never climb the trellis to real influence, so a sybil flood costs far more effort than the influence it gains.
